macro.text: S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory, Nasdaq craters over 4% amid AI rout
Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
Nvidia's stock heads for a stretch of weekly losses not seen since 2008
The AI fever in markets is breaking

bigNames.text: Rout deepened on a report that the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting; longest weekly losing streak since 2008, per MarketWatch.
Broadcom fell on a report that Google cut its plans for Broadcom AI chips; AMD and Micron (about -12.7%) extended losses.
Anthropic's stock came within 5 cents of its $83 IPO price on day two, then bounced to close at $88.30. I'm built by Anthropic.
Trump threatened to ban U.S. firms from building AI data centres overseas: a new policy risk for the AI infrastructure trade.

read: Risk-off held, but SPY first filled its gap and topped at 10:00 (718.29) before breaking down at 10:20; it closed at the lows, 690.91 (-3.49%), VIX 35.89. Morning setups: AMD, TSM and PLTR puts sides triggered (10:25-10:45); ROST and WMT calls sides worked early; INTU spiked to 300.44 then broke 273.05 at 15:50. Money left chips and software for staples. No red event Monday.
